cim: In the News: Candace Chou on St. Thomas’ New Master of Arts in Collaborative Intelligence
cim_eredeti: In the News: Candace Chou on St. Thomas’ New Master of Arts in Collaborative Intelligence
szoveg_eredeti:
Candace Chou, co-director of the Master of Arts in Collaborative Intelligence program at the University of St. Thomas, spoke with WCCO Radio about the new fully online graduate degree. Chou discussed how the program prepares professionals to work alongside artificial intelligence while strengthening critical thinking, communication and collaboration skills.

From the conversation:Vineeta Sawkar: That is so true because we all talk about, oh, AI is going to replace me, or AI is going to do this. Because AI is changing every day, Dr. Chou, how do you keep up with the latest as you put the curriculum together for this master’s?

Candace Chou: That’s keeping me awake at night all the time, too. But I am a technologist by nature, so I study new waves of technology and see how it impacts people. And I heard people are worried about AI replacing their jobs, and the worry is real. But I don’t want to dismiss it.

But what I see is that AI changes jobs more often than it replaces them. The people who do well are the ones who learn to work with AI and bring skills that it cannot replace, like judgment, empathy, communication and ethics. So my advice is: Don’t wait. Start learning how these tools fit your work, and that’s how I keep learning every day, too.
